WORDS+MAPPING: S1 Dataset https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article/file?type=supplementary&id=10.1371/journal.pone.0182845.s001 (SPSS .sav, sha256 d54a87460849ae2e218e0e59f4cb3d9d34993f9bb7a015e5fb2b2b1c06dacb56), variable labels and value labels of ses_1_1..ses_4_1. note: CODE DERIVATION: item IS the source column name (ses_1_1..ses_4_1 melted straight from the .sav), so there is no mapping step. WORDS: item_text = the .sav's German VARIABLE labels, option_text = its German VALUE labels, 4/4 items and 13/13 levels, copied verbatim incl. the file's casing and punctuation: ses_1_1 begins lowercase ('hast du ein eigenes Zimmer...') and ses_3_1 has no closing question mark; neither was corrected. The labels may be the study's data-file rendering rather than a character-exact copy of the printed questionnaire (no questionnaire is in the deposit or paper); none are at a truncation cap. ORDER NOTE: the .sav order is bedroom (ses_1_1, 0/1), vehicle (ses_2_1, 0-2), holidays (ses_3_1, 0-3), computers (ses_4_1, 0-3); the processing-script comment and the dictionary Description list 'car ownership, own bedroom, ...' in canonical FAS order, which is NOT the code order -- the labels and the per-item ranges both put bedroom at ses_1_1. CHECK (verify_schmidt_2017_fas.R, VERDICT: PASS): per-item x level counts .sav vs live identical -- ses_1_1 29/207, ses_2_1 19/111/106, ses_3_1 17/52/63/95, ses_4_1 1/39/80/113; live per-item n 236/236/227/233. The one ses_3_1=1.5 cell was dropped by the script as a data-entry error. LANGUAGE: administered in German (Bern, Switzerland; German labels; Swiss spelling 'Grösse' elsewhere in file). The paper prints only one English sample item, the canonical FAS II wording 'Does your family own a car, van or truck?' with 'no; yes, one; yes, two or more', which is not a translation of the administered 'Besitzt deine Familie ein Fahrzeug?' / 'Nein; Eines; Zwei und mehr als zwei' -- so it was NOT used; all _translated fields are this project's own translation of the German labels (machine_translation). instructions and section_prompt blank: no instruction text is published. STEP 3b clean: 4 items with ranges 0-1/0-2/0-3/0-3 are the FAS II block (paper: 'four questions ... cars, computers, number of family holidays in the past year, and having an own bedroom'; 'prosperity index (ranging from 0 to 9)'), not the PDS (pub_*) or PAQ-C in the same file. RIGHTS: FAS II is the HBSC study's scale (Currie et al.); no terms page restricting the items was found. The HBSC survey-protocols page (https://www.hbsc.org/publications/survey-protocols/, sha256 d58433084e066f14cd39946260ee4acebcdb52d924fc49513cac789725038e69, fetched 2026-09-10) states only that 'Public versions of HBSC research protocols have been made available for non-members since the 2009/10 survey' and that the current protocol needs registration (an access/tracking step for the document, not a stated fee, permission, NC, ND or no-redistribution clause). Silence = permission; wording shipped from the study's own CC BY deposit. No register row written (a round may not write ship rows) -- ship-shaped, flagged for the human per SKILL.md.

S1 Dataset https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article/file?type=supplementary&id=10.1371/journal.pone.0182845.s001 (SPSS .sav, sha256 d54a87460849ae2e218e0e59f4cb3d9d34993f9bb7a015e5fb2b2b1c06dacb56; variable labels and value labels of pub_1_1, pub_2_1, pub_3_1). Article XML https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article/file?id=10.1371/journal.pone.0182845&type=manuscript (sha256 919236f35becda4b8f8afedf59fbe53558093ed7514823935ec2e13b6554003f; Methods > Measures, Table 1). Processing script data/schmidt_2017_pds.py. Cached under itemtext/.cache/schmidt_2017_pds/.
note: CODE DERIVATION: item IS the source column name -- data/schmidt_2017_pds.py melts value_vars ['pub_1_1','pub_2_1','pub_3_1'] from the S1 .sav unchanged, so there is no mapping step; resp is the source numeric code unchanged (pd.read_spss convert_categoricals=False, filtered to integers 1-4, which drops the single 2.5 in pub_2_1). MAPPING (data_labels): the .sav's own VARIABLE labels (3/3) give the German item wording and its VALUE labels (4 levels x 3 items, 12/12) give the German option wording keyed to the codes 1-4 that the live table stores. Live per-item n via irw_table_sets 232/231/230 equals the source non-missing counts (pub_2_1 232 minus the dropped 2.5). Corroboration of both axes: (a) value labels are sex-consistent with the data -- pub_3_1 ('Hast du die Tage / Hat sich deine Stimme'): girls use only 1 'Nein' (111) or 4 'Ja' (12), boys only 1-3 (63/43/1), exactly a yes/no menarche item for girls and a graded voice-change item for boys; pub_2_1 ('Brüste / Barthaare'): boys 89 at 1, 19 at 2, 0 above, girls mostly 2-3; (b) the sum of the three items reproduces the paper's Table 1 pubertal status sum score: boys 4.13 (SD 1.06) vs published 4.11 (1.07), girls 5.44 (1.69) vs 5.43 (1.69), total 4.83 (1.57) vs 4.82 (1.57), and equals the file's own pub_index exactly -- so items are stored raw 1-4 as labelled. TEXT (study_materials, verbatim): item_text is the variable label verbatim, INCLUDING the authors' own trailing ellipses ('...' on items 1-2, '..' on item 3) -- these labels are the authors' abbreviated stems, well under SPSS's 255-char cap, not an SPSS truncation; the full administered German PDS stems (Watzlawik 2009, Diagnostica 55(1):55-65) are not in the deposit or paper and were not hunted off-source. option_text is the value labels verbatim, including the source typo 'fängt verzeinzelt an' (for 'vereinzelt') on pub_2_1 level 2, kept uncorrected. Items 2 and 3 are sex-specific pairs under one code (girls: breast growth / menstruation; boys: beard hair / voice), which the labels express with ' / '; shipped as the single label, disclosed in public_note. pub_3_1 levels 1 and 4 likewise combine the girls' yes/no answer with the boys' anchor ('Nein / Noch nicht verändert', 'Ja / Stimmbruch hinter mir'). The paper's English generic anchors ('not yet started (1 point); barely started (2 points); definitely started (3 points); seems complete (4 points)') and its sample boys' question ('Have you noticed a deepening of your voice?') differ from the item-specific value labels, so they were not used. instructions/section_prompt blank: no instruction text published. pub_2_1 level 4 has an option row though no respondent used it (live max 3) -- unused level, not a gap. TRANSLATION: all _translated fields are this project's English rendering of the German labels (machine_translation); 'die Tage haben' rendered as 'have your period'. Issues-page entry owed per the machine_translation rule. STEP 3b clean: 3 items on 1-4 are the PDS pub_* block, not the FAS II ses_* block (0-1/0-2/0-3; sibling schmidt_2017_fas). RIGHTS: no restriction located. Petersen et al. (1988) PDS: the Murdoch Children's LifeCourse measurement library (https://lifecourse.melbournechildrens.com/measurement-library/pds/) states 'The PDS is free to use and access'; parentingacrosscultures.org PDS page carries no terms; no fee, permission, NC, ND or redistribution clause found for the PDS or for Watzlawik's German version. instrument_rights_register.csv has no PDS row; per the 2026-09-10 rule this round does NOT write a ship row -- escalate to the round summary. Shipped wording is the study's own abbreviated labels from its CC BY 4.0 deposit.
public_note: Items pub_2_1 and pub_3_1 each hold two sex-specific questions under one code (girls: breast growth and menstruation; boys: beard growth and voice change), and the item text is the study's own abbreviated German data-file labels (ending in '...'), not the full questionnaire wording, with English translated by IRW.

source_ref: WORDS: Eurobarometer 38.1 (Nov 1992) Country Specific Questionnaire, United Kingdom, GESIS ZA2295_q_gb.pdf (https://access.gesis.org/dbk/8897, sha256 63d8b07cf97f1a41ec82dc5db38c93d6c01f49cfff0ce31f021c6e8911aa2586; scanned images, read visually), questionnaire pages -17- and -19- (PDF pp. 46, 48): SHOWCARD T2 Q.62 a/d/h/l and SHOWCARD U2 Q.66 a/d/k, the 4-point split-ballot version. CODES: ltm package Science.Rd (CRAN ltm; data source for the IRW table) lists each column name against its statement. ORIENTATION: Eurobarometer 38.1 codebook GESIS ZA2295_cdb.pdf v1.0.1, doi:10.4232/1.10904 (https://access.gesis.org/dbk/8888, sha256 2b7791b1b265090ddabcf4c3bdc4b53384af659c8cc201c4997a2f91a2878329), GB-GBN marginals for v249/v252/v256/v260/v294/v297/v304 (ballot B) and v237/v240/v244/v248/v283/v286/v293 (ballot A).
note: No processing script exists in data/ for this table (data/ltm.R covers WIRS/Mobility/LSAT/Abortion only); the live table is row-for-row identical to as.integer(ltm::Science) (checked: all 392x7 cells), and item codes ARE the ltm column names, so item<->item_text rests on Science.Rd listing each code with its statement (paper_explicit, self-describing codes). Item text transcribed from the GB questionnaire rather than the Rd; the two agree word for word except Benefit, where the Rd reads "any harmful effect" and the questionnaire (both ballots) and codebook read "effects" -- the questionnaire is shipped. Two section_ids because Q.62 and Q.66 carry different lead-in wording; both lead-ins transcribed verbatim, including the trailing "So firstly..." on Q.62. instructions left blank. RESPONSE ORIENTATION DEPARTS FROM THE TABLE DOCUMENTATION. ltm factor levels and the live table resp_raw say 1=strongly disagree..4=strongly agree for all seven items. The GB-GBN codebook marginals show that is true only for the four positively worded items: for Environment, Technology and Industry the live distribution matches the GB marginal only when read reversed (1=Strongly agree..4=Strongly disagree); total variation distance 0.034/0.027/0.023 reversed vs 0.370/0.436/0.701 as documented (e.g. Industry live 0.026/0.120/0.441/0.413 read SA..SD vs GB ballot B 0.030/0.124/0.456/0.390). The data are scored so that high = favourable to science on every item, as Bartholomew et al. presumably recoded; the ltm labels (and so resp_raw) were never updated. option_text is shipped in the verified orientation. See verify_science_ltm.R. Option labels are the questionnaire card labels (Strongly agree / Agree to some extent / Disagree to some extent / Strongly disagree), which the Rd also quotes; the ltm factor labels ("disagree", "agree") are shortened and not what respondents read. The survey had a split ballot: version A added "Neither agree nor disagree" and version B did not; the 4-category live data match B form, but marginals cannot exclude ballot A with neutral answers dropped (TVD to ballot A also small, 0.013-0.066). Item and option wording is otherwise identical across ballots; DK responses are absent from the data (ltm/LISREL: missing deleted beforehand). RIGHTS: Eurobarometer questionnaire is a European Commission survey instrument distributed openly by GESIS without registration; no fee, permission, non-commercial, no-derivatives or no-redistribution clause attached to the questionnaire wording was located (GESIS search pages were Cloudflare-walled, so the GESIS terms page itself was not read). Silence treated as permission; no register row written (rounds may not write ship rows).
public_note: For Environment, Technology and Industry (the three negatively worded statements) resp is reverse-scored relative to the ltm package documentation and to this table's resp_raw column: resp 4 means the respondent strongly DISAGREED with the statement as worded, which the Eurobarometer 38.1 Great Britain codebook marginals confirm (e.g. Industry: 39% strongly disagree in the survey vs 41% at resp 4 here), so option_text follows the data rather than resp_raw
